BERG-SPLITT, also known as non-explosive rock splitter, is a powerful cement-like powder that is mixed with water to split rock and stone without explosives…

BERG-SPLITT, also known as non-explosive rock splitter, is a powerful cement-like powder that is mixed with water to split rock and stone without explosives. The product is supplied in 20 kg steel buckets with 4 powder bags and is lime-based, which makes it ideal for sensitive environments where traditional blasting is not possible.
BERG-SPLITT works perfectly in confined spaces, close to buildings, in quarries or mines and requires no permits.
The product is available in two variants: one for temperatures between +10 °C and +25 °C and a winter variant for -5 °C to +10 °C (BERG-SPLITT Winter), which makes it usable all year round.
It is important to note that the temperature of the rock itself, not of the air, affects the performance of the product.

Preparation: Drill holes in the rock or stone to be split. The ideal hole diameter is between 30 mm and 48 mm, but it can also be larger (e.g. 60 mm). The spacing between holes should be 5–10 times the hole diameter, which means the holes are drilled about 35–40 cm apart for optimal splitting. If the hole diameter is smaller, the holes must be closer together.
Mixing: Pour 1.5 litres of water into a container and add 5 kg of Berg-Splitt powder (one bag from the 20 kg bucket) while stirring until you get a smooth, thin, lump-free mortar.
NOTE! At low temperatures use lukewarm water, at high temperatures use cold water.
Application: Pour the mixture directly into the pre-drilled holes. Then cover the area with a tarpaulin or similar to protect it from rain and direct sunlight.
Splitting: The rock usually cracks within 24 hours.
Consumption: The approximate consumption depends on the depth and diameter as shown below.
That is, holes that are 40 mm in diameter and 2.5 metres deep have the following consumption per hole:
2.1 kg / metre * 2.5 metres = 5.25 kg per hole

Brickcover® is a special impregnating agent that protects brick and stone against deterioration. Thanks to its special catalyst it penetrates deep into all absorbent materials and leaves the surface and appearance of the stone natural and unchanged. Brickcover® is non-toxic and leaves no surface film. The formula is based on potassium salt, which gives the treatment an extremely long service life, effective on both horizontal and vertical surfaces. Brickcover® penetrates the structure and allows the material to breathe normally. It protects the surface against deterioration and makes it resistant to freeze/thaw cycles. When applied correctly, the treatment is guaranteed for 8–10 years.
Ultimate protection against mould, bacteria, nitrates and salt efflorescence.
Allows the material to breathe normally.
Leaves no surface film and the appearance of the stone remains natural and unchanged.
Treatment guaranteed for 8–10 years when applied correctly.
Joints in swimming pools, showers, terraces etc.

Brickcover® must be applied to a completely clean and dry surface. Clean the surface thoroughly; it must be free from deposits of oil, paint and dust. Allow to dry until the surface is completely dry. Apply Brickcover® until the material is saturated, but without applying too much. Apply from the bottom upwards on vertical surfaces. Given the wide range of bricks available today, we recommend testing Brickcover® on a small sample area to verify working conditions.

Ercole® ECOACTIVE is a photocatalytic cement-based mix for coatings where reduced air pollution is desired. It can also be used where a small thickness is required. Ercole® ECOACTIVE triggers a chemical reaction that breaks down pollutants. Ercole® ECOACTIVE delivers over 60% reduction of pollutants, ensures the removal of particles and makes the air clean and fresh. Ercole® ECOACTIVE is safe and durable, waterproof and resistant. It can be used on concrete, wood and asphalt, both indoors and outdoors.
Works on both vertical and horizontal surfaces

Application
Mix with water (4–6 litres for self-levelling) until the desired consistency is reached. Vertical and ceiling surfaces require a stucco-like consistency. Mix with a hand drill or paddle mixer in a 20-litre bucket. For larger quantities a cement mixer can be used to advantage. Apply with a rubber squeegee, sprayer, trowel or similar. To achieve the desired effect, sanding can be done between layers and after the final result. Use sandpaper or a polishing machine.

EverCrete® Vetrofluid is a special impregnating agent that protects concrete from deterioration. The formula is based on water glass with a special catalyst, which allows the product to penetrate up to 40 mm into the concrete. It seals the pores of the concrete and becomes a permanent barrier.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid can be applied for permanent waterproofing and protection of all types of concrete – fresh, mature and for repairs.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid complies with the provisions of EC Directive 89/106 and meets the requirements of standard EN 1504-2.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid guarantees permanent waterproofing of concrete, even with negative pressure.

EverCrete® Vetrofluid gives concrete extraordinary resistance to freeze/thaw cycles and protects against chlorides, sulphates and de-icing salts. Even after 300 cycles of exposure to freezing and thawing, concrete treated with EverCrete® Vetrofluid is perfectly preserved and incredibly durable.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid is a permanent solution against carbonation and chloride ingress. It maintains a stable alkaline environment over time that fully protects the reinforcement.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid is certified for use in contact with drinking water and is an excellent barrier against chemical attack.

EverCrete® Vetrofluid blocks water / rising damp when used on the foundations of structures. It prevents the concrete from releasing cement dust into the environment, effectively prevents the ingress of pollutants and thus provides a healthier environment.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid is odourless, colourless and non-toxic.
EverCrete® Vetrofluid is a permanent and final treatment.

Everwood is an agent for protecting all types of wood from deterioration. It consists of water glass modified with a special catalyst. The product penetrates deep into the natural porosity of the wood and binds the wood fibres, forming a permanent barrier. Everwood effectively reduces the flammability of wood. It protects against termites and against the absorption of water and moisture. Everwood extends the durability of wood with all surface treatments.

Everwood is a permanent barrier that effectively prevents and reduces the amount of moisture in the timber (by at least 50%) and prevents the formation of mould, fungi, bacteria, termites and flames in the event of fire, which are the main causes of deterioration. It reduces the penetration of oils, grease and pollutants.

Everwood does not form a surface film but penetrates into the structure and allows the timber to breathe normally. It does not change the natural structure and colour of the wood; it is odourless and colourless.
Everwood increases hardness and therefore the resistance of timber to wear and freeze/thaw cycles over time.
Everwood considerably reduces the flammability of wood.
Everwood does not change the structure or the natural colour of the wood. It improves the adhesion of varnishes, dyes, paints and fillers in a uniform way and extends service life by 300%.
Everwood is non-toxic and environmentally friendly. It is therefore suitable for use in “green buildings”. If applied correctly, the treatment is guaranteed for 8–10 years.
All wood and timber, indoors and outdoors

Natural and untreated wooden surfaces require no preparation. Everwood must be applied at temperatures above 5 °C. All previous treatments or paint must be removed to ensure the effective penetration of Everwood. Shake well before use. Do not dilute or mix with any other liquid. Everwood should be applied with a low-pressure pump, roller or brush. Normal application requires only one treatment and the result depends on the porosity of the wood. Apply liberally to saturate the material. Apply from the bottom upwards on vertical walls.

Microbond is a cement-based micro-cement for renewing and protecting all types of surfaces. It consists of a one-component mix modified with special polymers and catalysts. The product is applied in an extremely thin layer and penetrates the porosity of the substrate to create a permanent and uniform surface. Microbond effectively reduces wear and abrasion of existing surfaces. It protects against water absorption and moisture, and resists scratches and abrasion. When Microbond is treated with Ecobeton’s protective sealers, the surface becomes completely waterproof and fire resistant according to class A standards.
Microbond thus extends the life of floors, walls, bathrooms and furniture with outstanding durability.
Coverage is 1.5 kg per m² (approx. 15–16 square metres per 25 kg bucket at a thickness of about 1 mm). For beginners, allow 1.5–2 kg per m².

Microbond is a permanent cement-based barrier for effectively protecting and renewing all types of surfaces (up to 1 mm thickness). It prevents water absorption, abrasion and scratches while resisting freeze/thaw cycles, which are the main causes of surface deterioration. It reduces the penetration of oils, grease and pollutants when treated with Ecobeton’s protective sealers.

Microbond does not form a surface film but penetrates the structure of the substrate and allows the surface to breathe normally. It does not change the natural appearance of the substrate but enhances it with a smooth, uniform texture. It is odourless and colourless in its basic form.
Microbond increases hardness and therefore the resistance of surfaces to wear and abrasion over time. It considerably reduces the fire risk and has been approved in class A tests.

Microbond does not change the structure or natural appearance of the substrate. It improves the adhesion of paints, varnishes and surface treatments in a uniform way and considerably extends service life. Microbond is non-toxic, environmentally friendly and has a very low VOC content, which makes it suitable for use in “green buildings”.
All types of floors, walls and ceilings, indoors and outdoors
Concrete, wood, metal, tiles and plaster
Bathroom surfaces, kitchens and wet rooms
Commercial surfaces such as bars, restaurants, showrooms

Surfaces must be structurally sound without cracks or defects. All previous treatment, paint or contaminants must be removed to ensure optimal adhesion. Microbond must be applied at substrate temperatures above 5 °C and air temperature above 10 °C, but not above 40 °C. Do not apply if precipitation is expected within 24 hours.

Shake well before use. Microbond is mixed only with clean water (5–7 litres per 25 kg) and mixed at low speed with a drill in a clean bucket until the desired consistency is reached. Wait 5 minutes before application. Do not dilute or mix with any other liquid.

Microbond should be applied with a filling knife, trowel or sprayer on a slightly dampened surface. Normal application requires two or more coats depending on the desired finish and the porosity of the substrate. Apply liberally to saturate the material. Wait 24 hours between coats. The surface can be sanded between coats to achieve an even finish. Apply from the bottom upwards on vertical walls.

Häny manufactures grouting and mixing systems. Take a look at their brochure below or contact us for more information.
Häny manufactures grouting and mixing systems. Take a look at their brochure below or contact us for more information.

For efficient mixing of cement, ultrafine cement and bentonite, Häny mixers create high shear forces with high-speed pumps and a unique vortex impeller. The pumps circulate the entire tank contents 2–4 times per minute, generating extreme turbulence and effective particle separation and ensuring complete hydration.
This intense hydration gives a stable and easily workable suspension, even for difficult-to-mix additives. The HCM mixer eliminates the need for pre-soaking of bentonite or storage tanks.

Häny’s vortex impeller has a large throughput (15–80 mm) and is extremely wear-resistant, which reduces wear and clogging. The HCM 300 and HCM 600 models can mix sandy grouts with particle sizes up to 8 mm. The maintenance-free shaft seal withstands dry running for several minutes without damage.

Unlike piston pumps, plunger pumps do not require close-fitting parts such as cylinders or precise piston seals. The plunger is sealed with a maintenance-free seal, and different diameters can be fitted to the ZMP 700 series pumps for flexible pressure and flow adaptation.

The injection valves are made of wear-resistant alloy steel with reversible valve seats. The hydraulic system provides a fast suction stroke that keeps the valves clean by flushing away heavy particles. The pumps also handle suspensions with a low water/cement ratio and a high sand content.

ZMP 700 pumps have valves for precise setting of maximum pressure. When the pressure is reached, the flow is adjusted automatically or stopped, while the pressure is maintained. Some models can be set from as low as 1 bar, which enables safe grouting in sensitive formations.

Built-in flow regulation allows the maximum flow to be set, which enables slow grouting in soft ground conditions without segregation or new voids. Together with the pressure control, the pumps can also be used for permeability tests.

It can often be a good idea to combine the pump with a silo to ensure an even and continuous supply of material. A silo reduces the handling of big bags, improves the workflow and can be fitted with a screw conveyor for automatic feeding to the pump. Rigs marked with P (e.g. MR-C 95P) stand for Power (or Performance, often in reference to extra powerful models). These rigs usually have higher engine power and are designed to handle heavier drilling work and deeper boreholes.

These rigs, which work with Kelly-bar systems and augers, are known for their versatility and robust performance. With drilling depths ranging from 18 metres to 32 metres and a maximum drilling diameter of up to 1,300 mm, the MR-P series is perfect for different types of ground conditions and projects.

Marini offers a wide range of wire saws for different types of quarry and rock work.

For granite and harder stones, Marini offers machines with variable wire speed controlled by an inverter. These machines are adapted to handle tougher stone materials and are used for both vertical and horizontal cuts. The machines can be easily positioned and have high precision thanks to electronic control of the wire speed. Machines with variable wire speed are designated GRAN in the model name.

For marble and similar softer stones in quarries, wire saws with fixed wire speed are used, such as saws designated MAR in the name, for example: MAR FIL SUPER SP, which has motors of 75 or 100 horsepower. These machines are ideal for precise cuts with even wire tension, and they can work on sloping surfaces and horizontal cuts near ground level.

HEM (Hydraulic Excavator Mount) is the most popular drilling attachment manufactured by TEI Rock Drills. The stable excavator base and the long boom together form an excellent drilling platform. HEM receives its hydraulic power from the excavator’s hammer circuit, so no extra hydraulic installation is required.

TEI uses exclusively its patented hydraulic drifters and feed systems in the HEM. These advanced drifters have Automatic Stroke Adjustment (ASA): when the drill string is not engaged the hammer goes into idle mode, and when the operator applies pressure to the drill string, ASA automatically brings the hammer up to full power. The built-in swivel accepts air, water or grout for all types of drilling, including installation of the popular hollow bars.

VibroDrill VD100 is the flagship of the VibroDrill series.

VibroDrill combines rotation with controlled vibration to drive the drill efficiently through difficult soil layers. It is used for foundation work and geotechnical works such as micropiles, self-drilling anchors and geothermal drilling. The vibration helps reduce resistance in the ground and gives a smoother drilling process with better control.
Feel free to take a look at the brochure below or contact us for more information.
• Versatility: from sand and clay to rock

VD100 is built for stability, performance and long service life. It is equipped with a built-in damping mechanism (rubber) that prevents vibrations from being transferred to the mast. This means less strain on the equipment, smoother drilling and better control in production.

With a drilling angle of 0° to 90°, VibroDrill VD100 can be used both vertically and horizontally – perfect for everything from classic foundation work to more advanced installations where access and geometry require flexibility. The operator can also adjust the eccentric moment to optimise performance depending on ground conditions.

VibroDrill VD100 is delivered as standard with 100 Hz, but can also be adapted to 85 Hz or 120 Hz depending on application and desired drilling behaviour. There are also two motor types to choose from depending on the torque–rotation ratio desired.

VibroDrill VD150 is the most powerful drilling system in the VibroDrill series.
VibroDrill VD150 – when you want maximum capacity
VD150 is the powerhouse of the series and is built for heavier jobs, larger dimensions and high production.
• Well suited for: larger foundation reinforcement projects, heavier geotechnical work and applications where you want extra power reserves
VibroDrill VD150 works with high-frequency vibration between 100 Hz and 120 Hz for optimal penetration.

VibroDrill is built for stability, performance and long service life. It is equipped with a built-in damping mechanism (rubber) that prevents vibrations from being transferred to the mast. This means less strain on the equipment, smoother drilling and better control in production.

With a drilling angle of 0° to 90°, VibroDrill VD150 can be used both vertically and horizontally – perfect for everything from classic foundation work to more advanced installations where access and geometry require flexibility. The operator can also adjust the eccentric moment to optimise performance depending on ground conditions.
VibroDrill VD150 is delivered as standard with 100 Hz, but can also be adapted to 85 Hz or 120 Hz depending on application and desired drilling behaviour.
The series consists of further drilling units, namely: VD50, VD100 and VD150.
Get in touch and we will tell you more about applications and which VibroDrill model (VD50, VD100 or VD150) suits your projects best.
VibroDrill VD50 is the most compact drilling system in the VibroDrill series.

VibroDrill VD50 combines rotation with controlled vibration to drive the drill efficiently through difficult soil layers. It is used for foundation work and geotechnical works such as micropiles, self-drilling anchors and geothermal drilling. The vibration helps reduce resistance in the ground and gives a smoother drilling process with better control.
VibroDrill VD50 – compact, fast and agile
VD50 is a strong choice for those who want vibratory drilling in a compact format, with a focus on agility and efficiency.
• Well suited for: medium-sized work with micropiles, anchors and geotechnics where access and flexibility are decisive
VibroDrill VD50 can be adapted to frequencies of 85 Hz, 100 Hz or 120 Hz depending on ground conditions and desired impact energy.

When the vibro is on, the clay is converted into a liquid mass resembling porridge. By breaking the structure of the clay, the skin friction around the drill or pile is almost completely eliminated, causing it to sink into the ground with minimal resistance. This technique maximises penetration speed and enables extremely efficient installation of sheet piles and piles in cohesive soils.
